{{Short description|Sporting competition}} {{refimprove|date=June 2020}} {{Use Irish English|date=March 2020}} {{Use dmy dates|date=March 2020}} {{Infobox GAA championship |image = |name = Munster Senior Hurling Championship |county = |province = Munster |year = 2020 |trophy = The Munster Cup |sponsor = |date = 25 October – 15 November 2020 |num_teams = 5 |defending_champions = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] |winners = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] |ordinal = 21 |manager = [[John Kiely (Limerick hurler)|John Kiely]] |captain = [[Declan Hannon]] |qualify_for = [[2020 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|Munster SHC Final]]
[[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland SHC]] |runnersup = [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] |runnerupmanager = [[Liam Cahill]] |runnerupcaptain = [[Conor Prunty]] |promoted = |relegated = |matches = 4 |total_scored = |poty = |topscorer = |website = |previous = [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship|2019]] |next = [[2021 Munster Senior Hurling Championship|2021]] }} The '''2020 Munster Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 133rd staging of the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] since its establishment by the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] in [[1888 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1888]]. The championship fixtures were announced on 10 October 2019, with the championship due to take place between 10 May and 28 June 2020. However, due to the [[impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on Gaelic games]], the draw for a rescheduled championship took place on 26 June 2020 with a new knock-out format being adopted,{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/2020-all-ireland-hurling-championship-draws-4845364-Oct2019/|title=All-Ireland champions Tipperary start out with trip to Waterford as 2020 hurling fixtures revealed|publisher=The 42|date=10 October 2020|accessdate=27 June 2020|first=Emma|last=Duffy}}{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/310982|title=2020 Leinster and Munster SHC draws: Holders Wexford and Limerick find out opponents|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=26 June 2020|accessdate=27 June 2020|first=|last=}} rescheduled to take place between 24/25 October and 14/15 November 2020. The championship format returned to the round-robin league in [[2022 Munster Senior Hurling Championship|2022]]. [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] were the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship|defending Munster champions]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|publisher=The 42|date=30 June 2019|accessdate=27 June 2020|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} They retained their title, beating Waterford in the final by 4 points. The same two teams went on to contest [[2020_All-Ireland_Senior_Hurling_Championship_final|the All-Ireland hurling final]] on 13 December, when Limerick won again, this time by 11 points. ==Teams== [[File:Semple1.jpg|thumb|[[Semple Stadium]]]] [[File:Páirc Uí Chaoimh.jpg|thumb|[[Páirc Uí Chaoimh]]]] [[File:Hurling game, Cusack Park, Ennis.jpg|thumb|[[Cusack Park (Ennis)|Cusack Park]]]] The Munster championship was contested by five of the six counties from the Irish province of [[Munster]].
